slice.hypothesis: A GitHub Issue stored in the same repository could act as a second durability/authority domain for role semantic state after the repository itself is deleted or deleted-and-recreated.
slice.tested_scope: GitHub Enterprise Cloud current documentation; same owner/repository-scoped Issue; threat event is deletion of the repository containing both Git objects and the Issue, with recovery required without assuming an explicit restore of the deleted repository. No live repository was deleted and no destructive experiment was performed.

primary_sources.observed: GitHub documents deleted repositories as a distinct deleted-repository object that can be restored within 90 days in eligible cases; restoration is the documented path to recover repository contents.
The Issues REST API is repository-scoped, and issue retrieval semantics are expressed relative to the repository containing the issue.

o_read_only_probe.scope_limit: This targeted negative search is not proof that O lacks every issue-related mechanism and is not generalized beyond the exact query.

observations: The candidate witness is repository-scoped rather than independently addressable outside the repository authority being threatened.

GitHub's documented recovery path after repository deletion is restoration of the deleted repository; this slice did not identify a guarantee that a same-repository Issue remains independently readable through deletion/recreation without that restore.
slice.inference: Within the tested threat model, a same-repository Issue cannot be credited as an independent second durability/authority domain. It shares the repository deletion boundary for availability and therefore does not close the previously identified same-authority-domain destruction residual.
slice.uncertainty: The result does not claim that GitHub loses all internal backups immediately, nor that explicit repository restoration cannot recover issues. It only rejects independence without relying on restoration of the same deleted repository.
